evidence.note: Repeatedly enumerates the full subsystem list (App/Pages routers, API routes, middleware, server actions, SSR, SSG, caching) and states intent to 'build systematically/incrementally' — identifies the major subsystems.
Creates src/{cli,plugin,runtime,shims} decomposition and orders work foundation-first: 'starting with package structure, CLI, and core plugin, then add features' — a dependency-sensible sequence.
Builds shims → router → SSR → config/middleware → main plugin in dependency order, with implicit/rough done-notions ('build the actual core plugin', 'get basic dev server working first').
Done-signal is loose and outcome-level ('run full test suite to see how many tests pass') rather than per-milestone test slices; no explicit maintained milestone artifact, no TodoWrite.

Work devolves into SSR/middleware debugging and an unrecoverable terminal freeze; SSG, use cache, server actions, hooks were never sequenced or reached — the initial plan was not re-sequenced or used adaptively, just abandoned into firefighting.

reasoning: The agent clearly identified the major subsystems and tackled them in a sensible foundation-first dependency order (CLI/plugin/shims/resolution and basic SSR before dependent features), with only a rough, implicit notion of when each piece was 'done' — squarely the level-5 description. It falls short of level 8 because there was no explicit, maintained milestone plan with concrete per-milestone done-signals tied to specific fixtures or test subsets (done-criteria were loose, outcome-level 'run the whole suite'), and the plan was authored/expressed early then abandoned into undirected debugging rather than re-sequenced adaptively, so it does not reach the 8-10 band.
